gates.title: Direction and decisions
gates.purpose: Settle the founder decisions that block later gates. Agents prepare briefs; only the founder decides.

steps.title: Independent fact-check of the decision briefs (a second agent session checks facts and sources)
steps.exit: A session that did not write the briefs checks every Verified and Reported claim in .agent/product-kit/briefs/ against its source, marks any it cannot confirm, and records PASS in the verify file. The briefs are drafted and do not block the founder's decisions.

steps.title: DECISION: product boundary - internal-only or also a public product
steps.exit: Founder decision recorded via 'decide' (the brief in briefs/G0.1-product-boundary.md is pre-drafted). If internal-only, also run 'ack NA-G10'. PRODUCT.md section 1 is edited only with founder approval.

steps.title: DECISION: ratify the Founder Operating Loop v1 release direction
steps.exit: Founder decision recorded; ROADMAP.md and PRODUCT.md updated to match. The Linear proposal must be read first; if it cannot be fetched, mark NOT READ.

steps.title: DECISION: infrastructure - hosting model, database, RPO/RTO, backup retention, budget
steps.exit: Founder decision recorded with concrete values for each field.

steps.title: DECISION: Sofia's name and title (COO or CEO)
steps.exit: Founder decision recorded. Any change to the COO boundary in PRODUCT.md is made only with the founder's approval and an ADR.

steps.title: DECISION: first AI employee roles, their order, and each role's autonomy ceiling
steps.exit: Founder decision recorded: which roles to hire first and in what order, with a maximum autonomy level per role. Each hire still needs its own approval (PRODUCT.md section 2).

steps.title: DECISION: autonomy policy limits - what Sofia may do alone, spend caps, public and customer-facing rules, deploy rules, kill-switch behaviour
steps.exit: Founder decision recorded with concrete numbers and rules for each action class in VISION.md section 6.

steps.title: DECISION: which provider to try first for live open-topic conversation, and the monthly voice budget
steps.exit: Founder decision recorded: the candidates to measure first and a monthly voice budget. The final provider is chosen from the G6.2 measurements. Options are in briefs/G0.4-identity-title-provider.md (provider section).

steps.title: DECISION: which product Sofia takes over first
steps.exit: Founder names the product. The persistence design calls Lumora 'Product 1 of SamJuniors'; confirm whether that is the one.

gates.title: Baseline integrity
gates.purpose: Make the repository trustworthy for agents and CI before anything new is built. No founder decision required.

steps.title: One canonical test command covering all test files, failing non-zero on any failure
steps.exit: A documented 'test' script runs every test file under tests/ (including .test.ts and the runner-specific suites); the exit code is 0 on a clean tree and non-zero when a test is deliberately broken; counts are printed; suites that only run under Bun are listed with the reason, per the runner divergence noted in PROGRESS.md.

steps.title: CI on pull requests: install, lint, typecheck, build, full tests, secret scan
steps.exit: Workflow runs on a PR and is green; a failing step blocks. Only 4 test files run in CI today.

steps.title: Full-history secret scan and classification of the 5 test-fixture hits
steps.exit: Scanner report over the full git history with every finding classified (fixture, revoked, or live); no unexplained finding; the chosen scanner and command are recorded so CI can reuse them.

steps.title: Reconcile documentation with code (voice status, README quickstart, SETUP.md)
steps.exit: Each contradiction listed with file evidence and resolved; no doc claims an unverified status; PROGRESS.md entry written.

steps.title: Honest fallback: a deterministic reply must never look like a live model reply
steps.exit: Reproduce on current main first. Fallback replies are visibly labelled in the UI and API; regression test added. If not reproducible, record evidence and close.

steps.title: Reproducible install: canonical package manager, clean-clone setup verified on Windows and Linux
steps.exit: Clean clone to running app verified in CI on Linux and by evidence on Windows; SETUP.md matches; the win32-only dependency handled per evidence.

gates.title: Persistence and deployment foundation (Phase 2.3C)
gates.purpose: Authoritative multi-instance persistence and a verified deploy path, per the approved Phase 2.3B design.

steps.title: Provision staging hosting and database per the infrastructure decision
steps.exit: Staging environment reachable; configuration recorded without secrets.

steps.title: Prisma to PostgreSQL with versioned migrations
steps.exit: prisma/migrations exists and applies cleanly to an empty database; schema matches the 2.3B design.

steps.title: Migrate file-backed stores (decisions, council, conversations, personal memory) with verified parity
steps.exit: Parity tests old vs new; rollback rehearsed; no data loss on a seeded dataset.

steps.title: Multi-instance concurrency: shared leases replace the PID guard
steps.exit: Two instances against one database pass the concurrency suite; the PID guard is no longer load-bearing.

steps.title: Backup and restore drill meeting the decided RPO/RTO
steps.exit: A real restore into a clean environment succeeded; measured RPO/RTO recorded against the decided targets.

steps.title: Deploy pipeline with post-deploy verification of the live environment
steps.exit: Pipeline deploys to staging and verifies the deployed environment, not just the local build.

steps.title: ADR: scale-later seams (owner-scoped keys, provider-neutral interfaces, no code that assumes exactly one human). Design only.
steps.exit: ADR approved by the founder; a checklist of existing stores and tables with their owner-scoping status; findings opened for gaps; no multi-founder feature is built (founder decision 2026-10-20).

gates.title: Security for real users
gates.purpose: Close known auth gaps and test against the agentic threat model.

steps.title: Close the two open auth gaps (live Clerk provisioning, gate.ts allowlist fix)
steps.exit: Both gaps reproduced, fixed, and covered by tests; unauthenticated calls to privileged routes fail closed.

steps.title: Threat model against the current OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications and LLM Top 10
steps.exit: Fetch the current official lists. Threat model against the OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications (ASI01-ASI10, Dec 2025) and the OWASP LLM Top 10 (2026 edition); use the OWASP Agent Control Standard (v0.1 preview) as a design reference only. Every risk maps to a control, a test, or an accepted risk signed off by the founder.

steps.title: Untrusted-ingress regression tests: transcripts, webhooks, tool output, screen text
steps.exit: Automated tests show injected instructions in each channel cannot trigger a side effect without the approval gate.

steps.title: Rate limits, request size limits, security headers and CSP, dependency audit in CI
steps.exit: Headers verified on a running build; limits tested; audit step in CI.

steps.title: Production secrets handling and rotation procedure
steps.exit: No secret reaches the client bundle (verified by scan); written rotation runbook tested once.

steps.title: Audit-log integrity, retention and deletion flows verified end to end
steps.exit: Tamper test fails closed; deletion flow leaves no resurrectable copy in any store. Include hash-chained or otherwise tamper-evident audit (none was found in the code on 2026-10-20).

gates.title: Single company brain
gates.purpose: One authoritative read/write path for company state and knowledge.

steps.title: Company Brain as the single read and write path; retire parallel legacy paths
steps.exit: Static and runtime proof that no code path reads or writes company state outside the Brain; old paths removed.

steps.title: First-class versioned Artifact model
steps.exit: Artifact model with versions, provenance and approval linkage; tests; no fabricated artifacts.

steps.title: GitHub adapter with idempotency key and unknown-outcome handling
steps.exit: Duplicate delivery produces one effect; unknown outcome is surfaced, not assumed; tests.

steps.title: Memory retrieval benchmark as a regression gate in CI
steps.exit: Existing benchmark runs in CI with a recorded baseline and a failing threshold.

gates.title: Memory system (personal, company, per-employee, persistent)
gates.purpose: Persistent memory that lets Sofia talk like one continuous person while keeping the personal and company scopes apart.

steps.title: ADR: memory architecture - scopes, partition and access rules, owner-scoped keys, provenance, confidence and supersession fields
steps.exit: ADR approved by the founder; scope-by-reader access matrix with a test plan; states that the Personal Mind and Company Brain stay partitioned (PRODUCT.md) and are read only through the routed, audited path; builds on the existing stores, adds no second store. Includes a comparison with Mem0, Graphiti, Letta and Cognee and a recorded borrow-or-adopt decision; adding a second store needs an ADR approved by the founder.

steps.title: Memory types and write policy: semantic facts, episodic summaries, procedural notes; consent rules; size and retention limits
steps.exit: Write-policy tests pass; unconfirmed candidates are never recalled as fact; personal memories keep the existing explicit-confirmation flow.

steps.title: Scope-aware retrieval: budgeted recall, ranking, source attribution, and an honest 'I do not remember'
steps.exit: Retrieval benchmark with a recorded baseline; every recalled item carries a source id; abstains when nothing relevant is found.

steps.title: Consolidation and forgetting: episodic into semantic, contradiction and supersession handling, deletion that removes derived copies
steps.exit: Tests show superseded facts are not recalled as current; after deletion no recall path (index, summary, embedding) returns the item.

steps.title: Role Brains: per-employee memory projected from the Company Brain plus the employee's own working and experience memory
steps.exit: Isolation tests: one employee cannot read another's working memory or the Personal Mind; projection is rebuilt deterministically from the Company Brain; a Role Brain never becomes company truth.

steps.title: Memory poisoning and cross-scope leakage tests
steps.exit: Automated tests show untrusted text cannot become trusted memory and personal facts never appear in company artifacts or employee context; failures close, not open.

steps.title: Continuity evaluation: remembers last week, invents nothing, survives restart and redeploy
steps.exit: Scripted multi-session evaluation with founder-approved pass thresholds, run before and after a restart.

gates.title: Decision engine
gates.purpose: Decides what Sofia does with each input. The model proposes; deterministic policy disposes. Extends the existing intent classifier; it must not create a second router.

steps.title: Decision contract and route taxonomy: converse, recall personal, recall company, research, use tool, delegate, schedule, ask to clarify, propose for approval, refuse
steps.exit: Typed schema and ADR that extend the existing intent kinds; every route lists entry conditions, allowed memory scopes and side-effect class; an unknown route fails closed to clarification. Compare against the existing intent kinds first; no second router.

steps.title: Router: model proposes a route with confidence, deterministic validation, deterministic fallback
steps.exit: Founder-reviewed labelled set; accuracy per route recorded; invalid model output falls back deterministically.

steps.title: Context assembly per route: choose memory scopes and budget, attach sources, enforce the Personal and Company partition
steps.exit: Tests show company questions never pull personal memory unless the founder asked, and every answer can list which scopes it read.

steps.title: Autonomy policy engine: deterministic table of action class x autonomy level x limits deciding auto, needs approval, or forbidden
steps.exit: Table-driven tests; the model cannot change the policy; changing a level requires a recorded founder decision. Compare with open-source policy layers (Latch, AgentPolicy, AgentLedger) and borrow rolling per-agent action budgets if they fit.

steps.title: Routing evaluation and calibration: reliability curve and Brier score per route; thresholds that trigger clarification
steps.exit: Report with a baseline and a CI regression threshold; low-confidence routes ask instead of acting.

steps.title: Decision log and explanation: inputs, route, confidence, policy result and outcome for every decision
steps.exit: Log schema and query; 'why did you do that' is answered from log entries that are cited; no log entry means no action.

steps.title: Kill switch and safe mode: one command by voice or panel freezes autonomous action and drops to read-only
steps.exit: Drill passes: stop works mid-run, workers halt, state is recorded; it also works with the model provider unavailable.

steps.title: Settings for autonomy and spend limits: editable in the app and enforced deterministically; with no value set, no autonomous model spend runs
steps.exit: A settings page edits the limits; a test proves an unset cap means no autonomous model spend and that lowering the cap stops a running task; every change is logged as a founder action. The founder said on 2026-10-20 that the daily spend cap will be adjusted in settings.

gates.title: Capability layer (tools, skills, MCP)
gates.purpose: One gateway through which every tool, skill and MCP server is registered, vetted, limited and audited.

steps.title: ADR: capability registry and single gateway. Every tool, skill and MCP server has a manifest and every call passes the policy engine
steps.exit: ADR and manifest schema (permissions, side-effect class, trust tier, version pin, cost); a static check proves no direct tool-call path exists. Compare with GitLab's AI Catalog pattern (versioned agents, flows and MCP servers with group controls) and OpenClaw's skill load precedence.

steps.title: MCP client behind the gateway on the current spec revision
steps.exit: Confirm the current spec revision and SDK at implementation time (2026-07-28 was the stable one when this was written); works with one real and one fake server; calls are self-contained; an audit record per call.

steps.title: Skills loader for the SKILL.md format: versioned, reviewed, loaded on demand; skills are instructions, never authority
steps.exit: Loads a skill by name and description; a skill cannot grant permissions; activation needs a review record; version pinned. Follow the open Agent Skills spec (agentskills.io); treat community skills as untrusted.

steps.title: Vetting and install pipeline for third-party tools, skills and MCP servers: provenance, permission review, sandbox, pin; no runtime self-install
steps.exit: Installing without founder confirmation is impossible; each item has a review record; community skills are treated as untrusted because malicious ones have been reported.

steps.title: Sandbox and egress control: least-privilege tools, network allowlists, secrets injected at call time and never shown to the model
steps.exit: Test shows a tool cannot reach a non-allowlisted host or read another tool's secret.

steps.title: First integrations chosen by the founder (for example email, calendar, social, payments, code host), each approval-by-default
steps.exit: Each integration has a contract test, a failure-mode test and a policy row; at least one side-effect integration passes unknown-outcome tests.

steps.title: Capability evaluation: contract tests, injection through tool output, cost caps
steps.exit: CI suite; instructions injected through tool output cannot trigger an unapproved action; a cost cap stops a runaway tool loop.

gates.title: AI workforce (employees Sofia manages)
gates.purpose: A real team: each employee has a charter, tools, a budget, its own memory and a record, all supervised by Sofia. A managed team, not a free swarm.

steps.title: ADR: employee model - identity and charter, permissions, Role Brain, budget, supervisor, performance record, version history
steps.exit: ADR approved by the founder; consistent with PRODUCT.md sections 7 and 8 (self-improving is not self-authorizing). Includes a comparison with Paperclip's org chart, budget hard-stop and pause/terminate model; adopting it would add a second orchestration engine and needs an ADR approved by the founder. The founder said on 2026-10-20 that Paperclip can be used for onboarding in future: the ADR must evaluate adopting it as the employee execution substrate and state the second-engine risk.

steps.title: Employee lifecycle: propose, founder approval, create, configure, evaluate, retire, with immutable versions and rollback
steps.exit: A test proves an employee cannot be created without founder approval; each version is inspectable; rollback restores the earlier behaviour.

steps.title: Delegation protocol: structured task (goal, boundaries, budget, deadline, acceptance criteria, scoped context) and structured result with evidence
steps.exit: Schema and tests; free-form agent-to-agent chat is not possible; every delegation is written to the decision log.

steps.title: Team topology rules: orchestrator-worker, bounded depth and fan-out, token and time budgets, effort scaling; single-threaded work for shared-context tasks such as coding
steps.exit: Fan-out and runaway tests; a budget stops a run in a test; a written rule says which task types run in parallel and which do not, backed by this system's own evaluations. Include a per-employee spend cap with a hard stop (not identified in the code on 2026-10-20).

steps.title: Per-employee identity and least privilege: own scoped credentials, tool allowlist and memory partition
steps.exit: Privilege tests: an employee cannot use another's tools or credentials; revocation is immediate.

steps.title: Per-role evaluation harness: task quality, cost per task, error rate, feeding autonomy decisions
steps.exit: Harness runs for every active role with a recorded baseline and regression gates.

steps.title: Hire employee 1 (role from G0.6) end to end, then stop and evaluate before hiring the next
steps.exit: One role live in supervised mode with its Role Brain, evaluation baseline and founder sign-off; a gate-style report before employee 2.

steps.title: Team view: what each employee is doing, status, cost and blockers, from authoritative state only
steps.exit: The panel shows only real state and matches the decision log; no simulated activity.

gates.title: Core loop v1 (Founder Operating Loop)
gates.purpose: The smallest end-to-end loop that delivers real value, with real data and real UX.

steps.title: Write acceptance journeys and success metrics for the v1 loop
steps.exit: Journeys in plain language with measurable success criteria, approved by the founder.

steps.title: UX flows for Cockpit, Decisions, Approvals and Activity including empty, loading and error states
steps.exit: Flows implemented against server state only; every state designed; no fabricated data.

steps.title: Implement the loop vertical slice end to end with real data
steps.exit: The journeys run against a real environment with real approvals and a real audit trail.

steps.title: End-to-end browser tests for every journey
steps.exit: Automated tests pass in CI for every journey; if the browser tool cannot launch, record why and use an alternative.

gates.title: Sofia live conversation
gates.purpose: Open-topic live voice that routes through the same governance pipeline. Voice never approves.

steps.title: Provider-neutral adapter for streamed open-topic conversation
steps.exit: Adapter behind the existing provider interfaces; works with one provider and a fake; no provider name in core logic.

steps.title: Streaming reply into speech with barge-in and a measured latency budget
steps.exit: End-to-end latency measured on Windows with p50 and p95 recorded; barge-in verified by test. Before building barge-in or turn detection, evaluate Pipecat and LiveKit Agents (VISION.md section 12) and record the decision.

steps.title: Route conversation and operational intents through one cognitive ingress
steps.exit: Single path proven by test; operational intents still pass classifier and gateway.

steps.title: Approvals only through panel or phone; voice can propose, never approve
steps.exit: A test proves a spoken approval cannot satisfy the approval gate.

steps.title: Panel fallback when voice is unavailable, with honest presence states
steps.exit: Every presence state designed and tested, including offline.

steps.title: Greeting on open, grounded in real state: time, last session, pending approvals, alerts. It never invents.
steps.exit: On opening the app Sofia greets within the latency budget using only real state; with no state she greets plainly; tested with empty and full state. First check whether any greeting behaviour already exists (NOT VERIFIED today).

steps.title: Persona specification and conversation-quality evaluation: natural, concise, consistent, no fabricated memories, one persona for COO and voice
steps.exit: Written persona spec approved by the founder; conversation evaluation with a recorded baseline; a fabricated-memory test fails the build.

steps.title: Proactive briefing: a short, interruptible summary of what changed since the last session
steps.exit: Briefing built from the decision log and approvals only; interruptible by voice; can be turned off.

gates.title: Windows node
gates.purpose: Authenticated local node: read-only first, then writes behind approval.

steps.title: ADR and threat model for the authenticated local node
steps.exit: ADR in doc/adr/ following the repo template; trust boundary and capability allowlist defined; node actions registered as capabilities behind the G14 gateway; founder approved.

steps.title: Read-only node: active window, window list, UI tree
steps.exit: Works on a real Windows machine; no write capability present in the build; audit record per call.

steps.title: Write actions (focus, invoke, type) each behind approval
steps.exit: Each action bound to an approved payload hash; denied without approval; tested on Windows.

steps.title: Vision fallback, sample-gated, only where the UI tree cannot identify the target
steps.exit: Sampling policy enforced and tested; frames not stored by default.

steps.title: Red-team: instructions embedded in screen content
steps.exit: Documented attempts and results; all fail to trigger an unapproved action, or the failure is a blocking finding.

steps.title: Design-system audit against the canonical visual language and fix drift
steps.exit: List of drift items with before/after evidence; tokens used consistently.

steps.title: Accessibility audit to WCAG 2.2 AA and fixes
steps.exit: Automated and manual keyboard and screen-reader checks recorded; no open AA failures on core journeys.

steps.title: Performance budgets enforced in CI (LCP, INP, CLS, JavaScript size)
steps.exit: Budgets set from measured baselines and enforced; core journeys meet LCP <= 2.5 s, INP <= 200 ms, CLS <= 0.1 on a mid-range test profile.

steps.title: Responsive layout and Android path decision (PWA or native client)
steps.exit: Decision brief approved by the founder; chosen path verified on a real device.

steps.title: Copy, empty states and error messages pass
steps.exit: Every error state states what happened and what to do; no raw errors shown.

steps.title: Observability: structured logs, metrics, error tracking, LLM cost tracking with caps
steps.exit: Dashboards or queries exist; a forced failure is visible; a spend cap stops a runaway loop in a test.

steps.title: SLOs, alerts, runbooks and incident response
steps.exit: Numeric targets approved by the founder; an alert fires in a drill; runbooks tested once.

steps.title: Failure-injection and load tests; repeat the restore drill
steps.exit: Results recorded; every failure fixed or accepted by the founder in writing.

steps.title: Operator documentation, onboarding and changelog
steps.exit: A new person can run the system from the docs alone, verified by a cold-start walkthrough.

steps.title: Release checklist run against QUALITY_BAR.md with evidence; go/no-go report
steps.exit: Every applicable QUALITY_BAR item has evidence or a signed exception; report delivered to the founder.

gates.title: Product ownership (Sofia runs a product end to end)
gates.purpose: Build, operate, market and support a real product under the autonomy ladder, starting supervised.

steps.title: DECISION: pilot charter - success metrics, budget and kill criteria for the product named in G0.9
steps.exit: Founder decision recorded with success metrics, a budget and conditions for stopping, for the product named in G0.9.

steps.title: Product as a first-class object: charter, goals, metrics, roadmap, owner, budget, risk tier, kill criteria
steps.exit: Model and tests; the pilot is created from it; no product state lives outside it.

steps.title: Build playbook: specification, implementation by a single-threaded coding agent, tests, review, deploy; production deploy behind founder approval
steps.exit: Runs on the pilot; CI gates apply; a deploy without approval is impossible. Evaluate OpenHands (MIT, sandboxed) as the engine for the Engineer employee and run it only inside its sandbox.

steps.title: Operate playbook: monitoring, incident triage, and changes through the same gates
steps.exit: A forced incident is detected, triaged and handled within the policy limits.

steps.title: Market playbook: positioning, content calendar, drafts in the brand voice, publishing only after approval, platform terms respected
steps.exit: Drafts produced for the pilot; nothing publishes without approval; brand voice is stored as memory.

steps.title: Support playbook: inbox triage, drafts, escalation, resolution; customer data minimised; replies approval-gated until graduated
steps.exit: Pilot support flow works with real or realistic tickets; personal data handling reviewed; whether customers must be told they are talking to an AI is reviewed by a qualified person.

steps.title: Closed loop: metrics, decisions, actions and measured outcomes feed the decision log and employee evaluations
steps.exit: One full loop demonstrated on the pilot with recorded before-and-after metrics.

steps.title: Autonomy graduation: raise a domain's level only by a recorded founder decision using evaluation evidence; spend caps; a kill-switch drill each time
steps.exit: Every level change has a decision record, evidence and a passed drill; no automatic promotion exists.

steps.title: Supervised pilot run for a founder-set period with weekly reports; go or no-go on wider autonomy
steps.exit: Report with outcomes, incidents, cost and open risks; founder decision recorded.

gates.title: Vision acceptance
gates.purpose: Prove the founder's vision, in the founder's own words, on the real system.

steps.title: Turn the acceptance scenarios in VISION.md section 10 into measurable pass criteria and get them approved
steps.exit: Founder-approved scenarios with a numeric or yes-no criterion each.

steps.title: Run every scenario on the real system; fix or accept with signed exceptions
steps.exit: Recorded results per scenario with evidence.

steps.title: Final report: each vision statement against its evidence, open risks, running cost, what remains; go or no-go for daily use
steps.exit: Report delivered; founder decision recorded.

gates.title: Public productization (conditional)
gates.conditional: Applies only if the G0.1 decision is public. If internal-only, run: node .agent/product-kit/kit.mjs ack NA-G10
gates.purpose: Everything a public product needs that an internal tool does not.

steps.title: Validate the narrow customer and problem with real users before building
steps.exit: Founder-run interviews or design partners with recorded findings; a narrow ICP and one problem statement approved.

steps.title: Multi-tenancy and data isolation with tests
steps.exit: Cross-tenant access tests fail closed; isolation verified at the data layer.

steps.title: Multi-user auth and role-based access
steps.exit: Roles enforced server-side; tests for privilege escalation.

steps.title: Billing, metering and per-tenant cost controls
steps.exit: Metered usage reconciles with provider cost; caps tested.

steps.title: Privacy policy, terms, data export and deletion; legal review by a qualified person
steps.exit: Documents reviewed by a qualified human; export and deletion tested.

steps.title: Support channel, status page and abuse controls
steps.exit: Status page live; abuse controls tested.

note: Gate and step IDs are stable names, not an ordering. Order of work comes from 'requires' and 'deps'; see the waves table in GATES.md.
